body.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and consider a pooled experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\). If \(((P_{r,\theta_r},D_r,\theta_r))_{r=1}^{K}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), then the pooled-law tuple \(\mathscr A_M((P_{r,\theta_r})_{r=1}^{K})\) identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed intervention-contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the truncated-factorization functional at \(V_{i_X}\).
body.justification: After the separate \(p\geq2\) graph-transfer theorem, this result uses \(p\geq3\) only to transfer an identified polynomial-CPCM law and graph to one treatment and two response contrasts.
body.gap: The published direct-law CPCM theorem identifies the DAG but neither unpools labeled type laws nor proves that the strict polynomial subclass's support, modular factorization, and moments make the designated contrast functional identifiable.
body.consumer: It states the intervention-effect output available to a prospective known-composition bulk assay after broad graph recovery, without extending finite-grid, certification, or Wald claims beyond the strict polynomial subclass.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a type \(r\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), and let \(V_r=(V_{r1},\ldots,V_{rp})\) denote a generic cellular vector with law \(P_{r,\theta_r}\).  The endogenous variables are the labeled count coordinates \(V_{r1},\ldots,V_{rp}\); the treatment is \(V_{r i_X}\), and the two outcomes are \(V_{r i_Y}\) and \(V_{r i_Z}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}three\text{-}designated\text{-}coordinates}\) and injectivity of \(\iota\) ensure that these three coordinates exist and are pairwise distinct.

First separate recovery of an observational law from identification of the causal contrast.  Let
\[
H(z)=(H_1(z),\ldots,H_J(z))^{\mathsf T},\qquad z\in(0,1]^p,
\]
be the vector of observable row probability generating functions.  Membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), the assumed equality \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), and \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}frontier}\) give
\[
\begin{pmatrix}G_1(z)\\ \vdots\\ G_K(z)\end{pmatrix}
=\mathscr R_M(H)(z)
=\exp\!\left\{M^+\log H(z)\right\},
\qquad z\in(0,1]^p. \tag{1}
\]
The logarithms in (1) are defined because \(z^{B_{ji}}>0\) pointwise on this domain and hence \(H_j(z)>0\).  The same theorem's probability-generating-function coefficient uniqueness conclusion therefore identifies each labeled observational law \(P_{r,\theta_r}\).  Equation (1) is an equality between an observable recovery functional and observational probability generating functions; it neither defines nor presupposes an intervention distribution.

By \(\mathrm{prop{:}polynomial\text{-}class\text{-}inclusion}\), every recovered component in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\) has full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), is causally sufficient, and lies in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\).  Since \(p\geq3\) implies \(p\geq2\), \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\) then identifies its labeled generating DAG \(D_r\).  This graph-recovery step uses neither the choice of \(i_X,i_Y,i_Z\) nor the intervention contrast; those enter only below.

Full support supplies the overlap needed to recover all observational kernels that occur after intervention.  For any vertex \(s\) and any parent configuration
\(a\in\mathbb N_0^{|\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)|}\), choose a complete vector \(v\in\mathbb N_0^p\) whose parent coordinates equal \(a\).  Full support gives \(P_{r,\theta_r}(V_r=v)>0\), whence
\[
P_{r,\theta_r}\!\left(V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a\right)
\geq P_{r,\theta_r}(V_r=v)>0. \tag{2}
\]
Consequently the identified law and identified graph determine, for every \(v_s\in\mathbb N_0\),
\[
p_{rs,\theta_r}(v_s\mid a)
=\frac{P_{r,\theta_r}\!\left(V_{rs}=v_s,
V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a\right)}
{P_{r,\theta_r}\!\left(V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a\right)}. \tag{3}
\]
The denominator is strictly positive by (2); when \(s\) is a root, the conditioning configuration is empty and its probability is one.  Thus no positivity condition is being silently imposed on only observationally occurring parent values: every finite parent configuration, including those induced by setting \(V_{r i_X}=1\) or \(2\), is covered by (2).

We next relate these observational kernels to the causal target.  Causal sufficiency and the acyclic CPCM semantics give a modular recursive system in a topological ordering of \(D_r\), with each node generated from its parents according to the kernel in (3) and with no latent common cause between node assignments.  Surgical intervention at \(V_{r i_X}\) replaces only that node's assignment by the constant \(x\in\{1,2\}\).  The chain rule in the resulting recursive system therefore gives
\[
Q_{r,x}(v_{-i_X})
:=P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=x)}(v_{-i_X})
=\prod_{s\ne i_X}
p_{rs,\theta_r}\!\left(v_s\mid
v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}\right)
\Big|_{v_{i_X}=x}. \tag{4}
\]
This is the truncated factorization in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}factorization\text{-}effect}\), now derived from the surgical-intervention semantics.  It is a probability mass function.  Indeed, its factors are nonnegative, so Tonelli's theorem permits iterated summation; summing the nonintervened vertices in reverse topological order removes at each step a terminal node's conditional mass function, whose sum is one.  After finitely many such steps, \(\sum_{v_{-i_X}}Q_{r,x}(v_{-i_X})=1\).

It remains to verify that the expectations defining the contrast are finite.  If \(N\mid\lambda\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\), then for every integer \(\ell\geq0\), direct summation yields
\[
\mathbb E[(N)_{\ell}\mid\lambda]
=\sum_{n=\ell}^{\infty}
\frac{n!}{(n-\ell)!}e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^n}{n!}
=\lambda^{\ell}, \tag{5}
\]
where \((N)_{\ell}=N(N-1)\cdots(N-\ell+1)\) and \((N)_0=1\).  The finite identity
\(N^m=\sum_{\ell=0}^{m}S(m,\ell)(N)_{\ell}\), where \(S(m,\ell)\) is a Stirling number of the second kind, shows from (5) that every conditional raw moment of \(N\) is a finite polynomial in \(\lambda\).

Under either intervention, the fixed coordinate \(V_{r i_X}=x\) has moments of every order.  Every nonintervened root has a positive finite Poisson rate by \(\mathrm{ass{:}poisson\text{-}root\text{-}positive\text{-}polynomial\text{-}dag}\), so (5) gives all of its moments.  Suppose inductively in a topological ordering that every parent of a nonintervened non-root \(s\) has moments of every order.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}poisson\text{-}root\text{-}positive\text{-}polynomial\text{-}dag}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}positive\text{-}exponents}\),
\[
\lambda_{rs,\theta_r}
=\alpha_{rs}+
\sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
b_{rsk}V_{rk}^{q_{sk}}, \tag{6}
\]
where all displayed coefficients are finite and every \(q_{sk}\) is a positive integer.  For an integer \(m\geq1\), put \(h=1+|\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)|\).  Convexity of \(t\mapsto t^m\) on \([0,\infty)\) gives
\[
\lambda_{rs,\theta_r}^{m}
\leq h^{m-1}\!\left(
\alpha_{rs}^{m}+
\sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
b_{rsk}^{m}V_{rk}^{m q_{sk}}
\right). \tag{7}
\]
The right-hand side has finite expectation by the induction hypothesis, also when one parent is the fixed intervention coordinate.  Equations (5)--(7) imply that \(V_{rs}\) has moments of every order.  Induction over the finite DAG proves, in particular,
\[
\sum_{v_{-i_X}}(v_{i_Y}+v_{i_Z})Q_{r,x}(v_{-i_X})<\infty,
\qquad x\in\{1,2\}. \tag{8}
\]

Define, only now, the observable-law functional
\[
\Phi_r(P_{r,\theta_r},D_r)
=\sum_{v_{-i_X}}(v_{i_Y},v_{i_Z})
\left\{
\prod_{s\ne i_X}p_{rs,\theta_r}\!\left(v_s\mid
v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}\right)\Big|_{v_{i_X}=2}
-
\prod_{s\ne i_X}p_{rs,\theta_r}\!\left(v_s\mid
v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}\right)\Big|_{v_{i_X}=1}
\right\}. \tag{9}
\]
Both sums in (9) are finite by (8).  Every kernel in (9) is identified by (3), and every graph index in (9) is identified by \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\); hence \(\Phi_r\) is determined by the pooled-law tuple through (1).  On the other hand, substituting the causally derived equality (4) into (9) proves, rather than defines, the equality
\[
\Phi_r(P_{r,\theta_r},D_r)
=\mathbb E_{P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=2)}}
[(V_{r i_Y},V_{r i_Z})]
-\mathbb E_{P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=1)}}
[(V_{r i_Y},V_{r i_Z})]
=\bigl(\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}\bigr). \tag{10}
\]
Applying (10) to each labeled type \(r=1,\ldots,K\) identifies \(\boldsymbol\tau\).  Thus the full-rank observable recovery map first identifies the component laws, the broad CPCM result identifies their labeled DAGs, and only the polynomial-CPCM support, modularity, and moment conditions are used to identify the fixed truncated-factorization intervention contrasts.
